sources.author: Jane Austen
sources.title: Emma
sources.locator: Volume I, chapters VI, XV–XVI; web extraction lines 330–380, 1162, 1169–1208
sources.read_extent: Selected passages of the primary novel, not whole novel
sources.access_method: web.open and web.find: readable primary text
sources.excerpt_locator: Volume I, chapter XV; web extraction line 1162
sources.supports: Elton’s proposal overturns Emma’s account; chapters VI and XVI allow comparison of the earlier portrait scene and later reconsideration.
sources.limitations: The manuscript’s account of possible reader participation is an interpretation, not documented audience data. The novel gives advance clues; it does not deceive every attentive reader.

sources.author: Stanley Fish
sources.title: Literature in the Reader: Affective Stylistics
sources.locator: Reprint pp.86–88; PDF page index 8–9. Relevant extraction lines 2506–2613 and 2812–2886.
sources.read_extent: Bounded primary passages, including the distinction between description and evaluation; not full article
sources.access_method: web.open and web.find: fragmented OCR of scan. Page marker 86 independently visible in extracted text.
sources.excerpt_locator: Reprint p.86; PDF page index 8; exact OCR fragments, extraction lines 2604–2609
sources.supports: Temporary failed interpretations remain part of the reading event rather than disappearing when final understanding arrives.
sources.limitations: OCR splits words and contains artifacts. The excerpt is retained exactly as returned; the manuscript paraphrases it. Fish’s descriptive proposal does not establish the revision’s evaluative premise. No clean full-text retrieval or screenshot inspection is claimed.

sources.author: Wolfgang Iser
sources.title: The Reading Process: A Phenomenological Approach
sources.locator: New Literary History 3(2), 1972, pp.279–299; passages pp.287 and 296
sources.read_extent: Indexed primary-page extracts at pp.287 and 296; not complete PDF
sources.access_method: web.search_query primary PDF extracts; direct web.open failed
sources.excerpt_locator: p.296, section V; line break preserved from primary PDF search extract
sources.supports: Anticipation and retrospection, and reader participation in the organization of a text, are close predecessors of the present idea.
sources.limitations: p.287 extract has truncated line endings. Only readable claims are used. This is not full-literature coverage or a priority determination.

sources.author: Neil Levy
sources.title: The Real Spoilers Puzzle
sources.locator: Sections 1 and 3 of publisher text; issue 2026, volume 1(1), pp.1–11; online 2025
sources.read_extent: Publisher-page indexed text of sections 1–3 and visible notes; not full publisher PDF
sources.access_method: web.search_query returned substantial publisher primary text; direct open returned 403/internal errors
sources.excerpt_locator: Section 3, paragraph beginning “The thought experiment suggests”
sources.supports: Autonomy account; section 1 also concedes twist and puzzle cases. The revision addresses a separate ground of regret, not a wholesale refutation.
sources.limitations: Empirical studies discussed by Levy were not separately audited and are not asserted as independent findings in the essay. Full PDF was not retrieved.

sources.author: Alon Chasid
sources.title: The Spoilers Puzzle
sources.read_extent: Primary author-manuscript indexed extracts; not full final publication
sources.excerpt_locator: Penultimate manuscript p.13, final visible paragraph
sources.supports: Distinction between known fictional truths and what current narration presents as true; imagining remains possible despite possible disruption.
sources.limitations: Attribution is explicitly to the penultimate manuscript. Final published wording and pp.10–15 as a whole were not checked.

sources.author: C. Thi Nguyen
sources.title: Autonomy and Aesthetic Engagement
sources.locator: Author manuscript abstract; supplementary indexed extracts at pp.6, 10, 12
sources.read_extent: Selected primary author-manuscript extracts; not complete paper
sources.supports: General precedent for valuing interpretive activity rather than only correct judgments.
sources.limitations: The new attribution is limited to the verified general thesis. The original specific attribution about helpful guidance was not independently recovered and is no longer asserted as Nguyen’s claim; the essay retains its own argument about assistance.

scope: Primary passages supporting revision. Not a full literature audit or novelty certificate.
